label: Search index alias
type: an alias pointing to one or more Full Text Indexes (or other aliases), merging their results - comparable to a filesystem symbolic link. Enables zero-downtime index rebuild/upgrade by letting a client-facing alias be repointed at a freshly-built clone while the old index keeps serving traffic.
aliases_note: Folds the OLD-generation (server/7.2/fts/fts-create-index-aliases.json) id into the id this round's own reading of the identical UI walkthrough (fts-create-index-aliases.md, unchanged since 7.2 apart from one seeAlso retarget) confirmed is the same mechanism round 22 had already promoted from search/index-aliases.md under this spelling - a genuine cross-generation duplicate, unlike its five sibling index-lifecycle pages (clone/delete/edit/system-indexes), which this round confirmed have NO search/ equivalent at all.
evidence: An index alias points to one or more Full Text Indexes or to additional aliases: its purpose is therefore somewhat comparable to that of a symbolic link in a filesystem.
Users can update/recreate/rebuild the indexes without interfering with the live systems by leveraging the index-alias feature.
relates_to_competency_question: Can a Search index be rebuilt or upgraded without downtime, and does that rely on the alias mechanism?
